title: Effective Batches & Activation Memory
description: Study global batch-size arithmetic, accumulation and loss normalization, activation recomputation policies, and sequence length and padding waste. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Global batch-size arithmetic
lessons.description: Compare two world sizes while keeping global batch size fixed.
lessons.conceptOverview: Effective batch size depends on local examples, data-parallel ranks, and accumulation steps. This arithmetic assumes the intended data partitioning and loss weighting. Changing world size without adjusting other settings changes optimization and may invalidate a speed comparison.
lessons.whyItMatters: Hold optimization conditions explicit when comparing distributed configurations.

lessons.title: Accumulation and loss normalization
lessons.description: Derive weights for microbatches of 8 and 2 examples.
lessons.conceptOverview: Accumulation sums gradients across microbatches before an optimizer step. Normalize losses according to the intended global mean, especially with unequal microbatch or token counts. Gradient synchronization frequency also affects performance and must match the accumulation design.
lessons.whyItMatters: Weight accumulated contributions by the intended example or token denominator.

lessons.title: Activation recomputation policies
lessons.description: Rank three model regions by memory saved and recomputation cost.
lessons.conceptOverview: Checkpointing selected regions saves activations and recomputes them during backward. The best boundary depends on activation size, recomputation cost, and execution behavior. Measure memory saved per added unit of compute rather than enabling every checkpoint indiscriminately.
lessons.whyItMatters: Choose recomputation boundaries using measured memory and compute tradeoffs.

lessons.title: Sequence length and padding waste
lessons.description: Compare total padded tokens with valid tokens for a length-mixed batch.
lessons.conceptOverview: Longer sequences increase activation and attention work, with scaling depending on the attention implementation. Padding adds positions that may consume compute even if their loss is masked. Length-aware batching improves utilization but should preserve appropriate sampling and shuffling.
lessons.whyItMatters: Measure padding and length distribution when explaining memory or throughput.
